rationale: Performance-critical SQL/query SHAPES whose regression is SEMANTICALLY INVISIBLE: a revert returns byte-identical results, so no unit/integration test can catch it, and an EXPLAIN-plan assertion is unreliable on small test fixtures (Postgres seq-scans tiny tables regardless of query shape). The only reliable mechanical guard is a source-substring assertion that the efficient shape is still present. These live in upstream-shaped files that upstream actively churns, so an upstream merge (or a well-meaning 'simplify' refactor) can silently restore the slow form with all tests green. Single source of truth read by both scripts/preflight.sh (perf query-shape sentinel section, always) and .github/workflows/upstream-merge-pr-shape.yml (on merge/upstream-* PRs). If you intentionally change one of these shapes to a DIFFERENT efficient form, update the must_contain anchors in the SAME commit (and re-measure) — do NOT silently delete entries to make the gate pass.

sentinels.rationale: GetLatestUsedAtByUserIDs feeds /admin/users and is called unconditionally on every Users-page load. It MUST stay a per-user LATERAL MAX so each user resolves via an Index Only Scan Backward on idx_usage_logs_user_created. Reverting to `SELECT user_id, MAX(created_at) ... WHERE user_id = ANY($1) GROUP BY user_id` makes Postgres full Seq-Scan usage_logs (prod: 2.4M rows / 2.3 GB → ~1.3s vs ~0.4ms — measured in PR #877). The revert is semantically identical (same returned map), so the integration test TestGetLatestUsedAtByUserIDs_UsesUsageLogs stays green either way — this sentinel is the only thing that catches the perf regression.

usage_dashboard_group_daily has one user-visible responsibility: Dashboard/Usage group distribution. GetGroupStatsWithFilters must retain getGroupStatsFromRollup for completed-day requests/tokens/cost distribution plus raw boundary spans, while the Groups Today/Yesterday/Total summary must not regain a second owner in this TK file.

GetAllGroupUsageSummary has one owner: usage_group_daily_rollups plus usage_group_rollup_state. The canonical owner composes published historical buckets with the retained raw tail and invalidates on source changes. A TK-first dispatch would recreate two lifecycle state machines for the same Today/Yesterday/Total numbers.

Admin Usage endpoint distribution must be able to load only the visible dimension (inbound, upstream, or path). The legacy default still computes all three for compatibility, so a refactor can silently remove the single-source gate while default-response tests stay green and the UI falls back to the previous expensive three-query endpoint chart path. These anchors pin the branch points that skip the non-visible endpoint group-bys.

The Dashboard/Usage group-distribution path uses completed-day usage_dashboard_group_daily metrics plus raw boundary spans, gated by groupDailyMetricsBackfilled so old cost-only rows are never trusted for requests/tokens. Dropping the bounds, raw split, or metrics-backfill gate would double-count or silently return zero historical metrics.

The Dashboard/Usage per-(group,day) distribution feeder and historical metric backfills. backfillGroupDailyAllOnce covers pre-deploy requests/tokens/costs; backfillGroupDailyMetricsAllOnce upgrades deployments that had the old cost-only table. Removing either backfill permanently undercounts wide-window charts or forces slow raw scans.

must_contain: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS total_requests
ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS account_cost
sentinels.rationale: Schema bridge for old deployments that already ran tk_038 with actual_cost only. Dashboard/Usage group distribution needs requests, tokens, total_cost and account_cost; without tk_046 the Go feeder/read path cannot use usage_dashboard_group_daily safely after rollout. Pins the additive migration so the performance fix is deployable on prod, not just fresh databases.

must_contain: has no finite timestamptz upper bound
has no finite timestamptz lower bound
sentinels.rationale: Partition retention must use PostgreSQL's declared exclusive upper bound, never max(data) or a filename suffix. This preserves empty future partitions, reclaims empty expired partitions, handles legacy names, and fails before any DROP when a finite time bound cannot be proven. A data-based regression can delete newly provisioned empty partitions immediately while every populated-partition test stays green. ListStraddling must also prune children whose declared lower bound is at/after cutoff before issuing min(created_at), or daily partitioning creates one cleanup round-trip per current/future day.

Each partitioned cleanup first drops only fully expired bounds, then caps row-level reclaim from a surviving wide legacy partition that still contains expired rows. Batches must sort by the retention time column and then ID so the existing composite time index is used; reverting to ID-only ordering scans and sorts nearly the full legacy wide partition, returns the same result, but runs until the overall cleanup timeout. The SQL LIMIT must use min(batchSize, remaining), not merely stop after a full batch, or the advertised hard cap can overshoot by almost one batch. Removing either bound-driven call or the exact remaining-budget clamp can yield green cleanup heartbeats while disk or lock pressure exceeds the online-safety contract. The shared cleanup heartbeat must also report usage_logs and billing-dedup states now that OpsCleanupService owns those datasets; without the fields, a lifecycle run can look green while omitting the newly transferred owners from its operator-visible result. Partition provisioning is separately guarded by the shared partitionmaintenance owner.

Alert-event retention must use fired_at, the event-time column already indexed and used by alert queries. Using created_at with the shared time-ordered cleanup batch has no supporting index, so a large expired backlog must be sorted before LIMIT and can recreate the cleanup timeout this registry guards against.

must_contain: SELECT COUNT(*) AS affected, MIN(created_at) AS earliest_deleted_at
sentinels.rationale: Partitioned usage_logs reclaim shares the online-safety hard cap and unified fail-closed heartbeat contract. Its SQL LIMIT must use the remaining row budget, and a missing straddling relation must surface as an error rather than being silently reported as successful cleanup.

Ops partition maintenance owns only ops_system_logs, ops_error_logs, and usage_logs. qa_records UTC-hour lifecycle must stay in observability/qa/lifecycle; reintroducing qa_records targets or monthly rehome staging here silently revives the retired copy/move path.
qa_records hourly provisioning and catalog-bound DROP must stay centralized; rehome/staging symbols here would revive the retired monthly copy/move lifecycle.

The QA lifecycle library provisions future hourly partitions and exposes maintenance-only committed-hour DROP plus bounded post-DROP cleanup recovery. Rehome/staging or fixed-age boundary symbols here would bypass the capture-seal, raw-commit, restore-verification, and lock-time recheck contract.

buildSnapshotV2Response MUST compute its sections (stats / trend / models / groups / users_trend) CONCURRENTLY via errgroup. Reverting to the sequential if-blocks returns byte-identical output, so no unit/integration test catches it, but the 30-day admin dashboard regresses from ~max-of-sections back to ~sum-of-sections (users-trend alone is ~6.6s cold on prod), and folding users-trend into this single endpoint turns from a one-round-trip win into an ~8.6s serialization. This handler is upstream-owned and churned, so an upstream merge or refactor that restores the sequential form silently re-introduces the regression — this substring is the only mechanical guard.

Admin Usage list/stats must honor start_ts/end_ts absolute windows before legacy start_date/end_date expansion. Dropping this silently widens the default rolling windows back to local date boundaries and restores the production /admin/usage/stats latency problem while returning semantically similar data. This upstream-shaped handler needs a source anchor so future merges cannot compile green after removing the absolute-window filter contract.

ListAffiliateInvite/Rebate/TransferRecords MUST use COUNT(*) OVER() instead of a separate COUNT(*) query before the paginated SELECT. Reverting to dual sequential queries returns byte-identical pagination totals but doubles DB round-trips (~780ms → ~400ms TTFB on /admin/affiliates/transfers). affiliate_repo.go is upstream-shaped and churned; integration tests do not assert query shape, so this substring is the only mechanical guard.

must_contain: g.Go(func() error { usageData = h.buildUsageData(gctx, apiKey.ID); return nil })
sentinels.rationale: GatewayHandler.Usage (/key-usage) MUST parallelize buildUsageData, buildAPIKeyDailyUsage, and GetAPIKeyModelStats via errgroup.WithContext. Reverting to sequential calls returns byte-identical JSON but restores ~612ms TTFB (~250ms when parallel). gateway_handler.go is upstream-owned; no test asserts concurrency shape, so this call-site substring is the mechanical guard.
